title: Mowgli's Brothers
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
One night, a hungry tiger named Shere Khan came near a family of wolves. He was hunting people, but the human family escaped. Their baby crawled into the wolves’ cave. Mother Wolf called him Mowgli and protected him. Shere Khan returned and demanded the child. Mother Wolf refused. She said the baby belonged with her family now. Father Wolf agreed to raise him.

At the wolves’ meeting, Shere Khan argued that Mowgli should be given back. The young wolf leader listened. Under the Law of the Jungle, two members of the pack could speak for a cub who had no wolf parents. Baloo, a brown bear who taught the cubs, promised to teach Mowgli. Bagheera, a black panther, offered a freshly killed bull as a gift. The pack accepted the boy.

Mowgli grew up among the wolves. Baloo taught him the words and rules that helped animals live together. Bagheera showed him how to watch, listen, and move quietly. Mowgli learned quickly, but Shere Khan still hated him. The tiger waited for a chance to take him.

When Mowgli was older, Bagheera warned him that the pack’s old leader was becoming weak. Shere Khan was persuading younger wolves to forget their laws. Mowgli needed to face the danger. Bagheera told him to bring the red flower from the village, because fire frightened the animals. Mowgli went toward the human homes. He did not know whether he would stay with the wolves forever, but he knew that he had to protect the family that had raised him.

title: Kaa’s Hunting
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
Mowgli had gone looking for excitement, even though Baloo had warned him not to trust the Bandar-log, the noisy monkeys. The monkeys had no laws and often made promises they forgot. They watched Mowgli while he was alone, then carried him high into the trees. Mowgli called to them, but they only laughed and ran across the branches.

The monkeys took Mowgli to an old place among broken buildings. They wanted him to teach them how to build shelters and make plans. Mowgli knew they had taken him against his will. He tried to stay calm and sent a message through birds to Baloo and Bagheera. The two friends hurried after him, but the monkeys moved too quickly through the trees.

Baloo and Bagheera knew they needed help. They found Kaa, a very large python who could climb and move silently. Kaa listened to their story. The monkeys were afraid of him, but he agreed to help because Mowgli was in danger. Together they reached the old buildings. Baloo and Bagheera distracted the monkeys while Kaa climbed over the walls.

Kaa moved his body in a slow, powerful pattern. The monkeys could not stop watching him. They became confused and lost their courage. Kaa found Mowgli and carried him away from the ruins. Baloo and Bagheera followed. Mowgli was tired and sore, but safe. His friends reminded him that curiosity was not a reason to ignore every warning. Mowgli understood that his choices had put them all in danger, and he thanked them for coming.

title: Tiger! Tiger!
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
After Mowgli was sent away from the wolf pack, he walked to a human village. The villagers were surprised by the boy from the forest. Messua welcomed him because he looked like the son she had lost. Mowgli stayed in her home and began to learn human ways. He wore clothes, ate meals at a table, and practiced the village language. He was kind to Messua, but village life felt strange to him.

The villagers asked Mowgli to watch their cattle. While he was away, Buldeo told stories about Shere Khan, the tiger who hunted nearby. Mowgli already knew the tiger and learned that Shere Khan still planned to kill him. He spoke with his wolf brothers and made a plan. The cattle would enter a narrow valley from both ends and trap the tiger.

Shere Khan was resting in the valley after eating. Mowgli and the wolves led the herds toward him. The frightened cattle rushed forward, and the tiger could not escape. Mowgli found that the danger had ended. He took the tiger’s skin as proof that Shere Khan would not threaten him again.

When Mowgli carried the skin into the village, the people became afraid. They thought he had used magic and chased him away. Messua had cared for him, but she could not change the villagers’ minds. Mowgli returned to the forest with his wolf brothers. He had learned how humans lived, yet their fear meant he could not stay. He would have to decide later where he belonged.

title: The White Seal
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
Kotick was a young seal born on an island where many seals gathered each year. He was different from the others because his fur was white. At first, the other seals stared at him, but his mother cared for him. Kotick grew strong and enjoyed swimming in the sea.

One day he saw hunters arrive. They drove seals across the beach and killed many for their skins. Kotick was shocked. He tried to warn the other seals, but the adults believed that the hunting would always happen. They told him that the island was their home and that he should stop worrying.

Kotick could not accept this answer. He traveled through the ocean to look for a safe place. He met many sea animals and visited faraway shores. Some beaches were beautiful, but people came there too. Kotick kept going. He learned how to swim through deep water and how to find food in different places. The journey was long, and more than once he wondered whether a safe island existed.

At last Kotick found a hidden beach protected by rocks and difficult waves. People could not easily reach it. He returned to his home island and told the other seals what he had discovered. They did not believe him immediately. Kotick challenged them to follow him and see for themselves. The seals swam behind him across the sea. When they reached the quiet beach, they understood why he had kept searching. Kotick had found a place where their young could grow without hunters.

title: Down the Rabbit-Hole
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
Alice was sitting outside with her sister when she saw a white rabbit hurry past. The rabbit wore a waistcoat and looked at a watch. It worried aloud that it was late. Alice had never seen an animal act this way. She followed it across a field and down a large rabbit hole. The hole went deep into the earth. Alice fell slowly past shelves and pictures, wondering where she would land.

At last she reached a room with many doors. They were all locked. On a glass table she found a tiny golden key. It opened a small door, but the doorway was too low for Alice. Through it she saw a lovely garden. She wanted to go there, but she could not fit through the opening.

Then Alice noticed a bottle marked “DRINK ME.” She checked it carefully and found no warning. After one drink, she began to shrink. Soon she was small enough for the little door, but she had left the key on the table above her. She could not reach it. A cake marked “EAT ME” made her grow very tall. Now the key was close, but the doorway was far too small.

Alice felt confused and began to cry. Her tears formed a pool on the floor. She was changing size again and trying to understand the strange rules of this place. The rabbit hole had brought her somewhere that seemed like a dream, but every new choice created a new problem. Alice waited. Alice waited.

title: The Pool of Tears
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
Alice grew so tall that her head touched the ceiling. She felt unhappy and cried again. Soon the room filled with water from her tears. When she began to shrink, she slipped into the pool and swam toward a dry place. She met a mouse in the water and tried to speak politely. The mouse was not pleased when she mentioned cats, so Alice changed the subject.

More animals joined them. They included a duck, a dodo, a lory, and an eaglet. They all needed to get out of the water. On the bank, the dodo announced that they should hold a race to dry themselves. There was no starting line, and everyone ran whenever they liked. They ran around in a circle until they were dry.

The dodo said that the race was over and asked who had won. The group could not agree. The dodo decided that everyone had won. Alice gave each animal a small sweet from her pocket as a prize. She had no idea whether the rules made sense, but the animals were pleased.

The mouse began to tell a story about a dog and a person who disliked cats. Alice tried to listen, yet she kept thinking about Dinah, her own cat. She mentioned Dinah’s hunting, and the animals became nervous. They slowly left Alice alone. She had meant to share a familiar thought, but it reminded her new friends of something they feared. Alice continued toward the garden, now wondering how easily a careless word could change a conversation.

After climbing out of the pool, Alice and the animals stood on the bank. They were cold and wet. The dodo suggested a race to help them dry. He marked no starting point and gave no clear directions. The mouse then offered to tell a story. He wanted to explain why he was annoyed with a dog and a person. Alice tried to listen carefully. The mouse told it in a serious way, but Alice could not follow all of it. She asked questions and sometimes thought of other things. When she mentioned Dinah, her cat, the animals became uncomfortable. Alice praised Dinah for catching mice, and the mouse hurried away.

Alice had not meant to be rude. She had simply forgotten that the animals might fear the animal she loved. Once they left, she felt alone again. The race had been fun because everyone could join, but the story showed how difficult it could be to understand someone from a different life. Alice continued her journey and tried to pay closer attention to what others were saying.

title: The Ass and the Grasshopper
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
An ass heard a grasshopper singing in the field. The music sounded light and beautiful. The ass asked what the grasshopper ate to make such a lovely song. The grasshopper said that it lived on dew, the tiny drops of water found on leaves in the morning.

title: The Wolf and the Crane
author: LessonCaptain (retelling)
summary:
A wolf ate too quickly and got a bone stuck in his throat. He could not remove it with his paws, and the bone hurt when he swallowed. author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Jim Hawkins lives with his parents at the Admiral Benbow inn. One day, an old sailor called Billy Bones arrives with a heavy sea chest. He pays Jim to watch for a one-legged sailor, but he gives little explanation. Billy drinks heavily, frightens the guests with sea stories, and behaves rudely toward Jim’s father. Dr. Livesey warns Billy that his drinking is damaging his health and that his threats will have consequences.

A sailor named Black Dog later comes to the inn and asks for Billy. The two men argue and fight. Black Dog escapes, but Billy collapses after the struggle. Dr. Livesey treats him and warns him again about alcohol. Soon after, Billy receives a black spot, a warning from his former shipmates. Jim and his mother realize that the pirates may return. They search Billy’s room for money owed to the inn, but they do not take more than the debt. Jim finds a packet among Billy’s papers.

Blind Pew and other pirates arrive at night, searching for the packet. Jim and his mother escape with the papers just before the men surround the inn. Pew is knocked down during the pirates’ hurried escape and dies. Jim takes the packet to Dr. Livesey and Squire Trelawney. Inside, they find a map made by Captain Flint. It shows where the pirate’s treasure is buried. Trelawney decides to prepare a ship and sail for the island. Jim is excited, but he knows the map has already brought danger to his home.

 The adults around Jim do not all respond to danger in the same way. The doctor tries to stay calm and ask useful questions, while the squire is enthusiastic and sometimes careless. Captain Smollett is cautious because he must protect the whole crew. Jim watches these differences and slowly learns that confidence is not the same as good judgment. The map gives everyone a reason to travel, but it cannot tell them whom to trust. Billy Bones’s warnings, the black spot, and the sudden appearance of the hidden map have made ordinary life impossible. Jim’s courage grows through observation: he notices what adults miss, remembers important details, and shares information when it matters.

title: The Sea-cook: Chapters VII–XII
originalTitles: VIII. At the Sign of the Spy-glass
XI. What I Heard in the Apple-Barrel
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Jim travels to Bristol with Dr. Livesey and Squire Trelawney to join their ship, the Hispaniola. Trelawney has bought the vessel and hired its crew. At the Spy-glass inn, Jim meets Long John Silver, the one-legged cook. Silver is cheerful and helpful, and he knows many sailors. He tells Jim that he has not heard of the one-legged man Billy feared. Jim thinks Silver may be trustworthy.

Captain Smollett is less confident. He dislikes the crew’s attitudes, the way the ship is loaded, and the fact that people know their destination. He asks the squire to move the weapons and powder to a safer part of the ship. Trelawney is annoyed by the captain’s suspicion, but Dr. Livesey listens to the concerns. The Hispaniola sets sail for the island.

During the voyage, Jim sees that Silver works hard and treats the sailors warmly. But one night, while he is hidden in an apple barrel, Jim hears Silver talking with other crew members. Silver explains that he once served under Captain Flint and knows about the treasure. He is helping the honest passengers for now, but he plans to lead a mutiny after the treasure is found. Jim is shocked. He understands that Silver’s friendliness has concealed a dangerous plan.

Jim tells Captain Smollett, Dr. Livesey, and Squire Trelawney what he heard. They now know that many sailors are pirates. They cannot openly confront Silver because the crew could take control of the ship. Instead, they quietly identify the sailors they can trust and prepare to defend themselves. The island is near, and the voyage has become a contest of patience and planning.

 The ship carries more than passengers and supplies; it carries competing plans. Jim has not yet told the adults everything he heard, and each delay matters because the crew is approaching its destination. Captain Smollett’s concerns now seem less like bad temper and more like careful preparation. Dr. Livesey and Trelawney must work together even though they do not always agree. Jim sees how quickly a friendly conversation can change when someone has hidden intentions. The apple barrel gives him a safe place to listen, but what he learns makes him less safe afterward. He cannot solve the problem alone, so he brings the warning to the people who can plan. Their quiet response shows that careful teamwork may be more useful than a dramatic confrontation.

Jim returns to his friends, who have moved into a wooden stockade. The doctor, squire, captain, and a few loyal sailors prepare for an attack. The doctor goes to speak with Silver, who offers a deal: give him the map and let his men take the ship, or face a fight. The captain refuses. Silver leaves, and the pirates attack the stockade. The defenders hold their position, although some people are injured and one of the loyal men dies.

Afterward, Jim leaves the stockade without telling the others. He finds Ben Gunn’s small boat and makes his way to the Hispaniola. The ship is no longer safely anchored. Jim boards it and discovers two pirates aboard. One is dead; the other, Israel Hands, is injured. Hands asks Jim to help sail the ship, but he secretly plans to attack him. Jim understands the risk but needs to get the vessel away from the mutineers. He must rely on his own judgment now, while the others remain at the stockade.

Ben hints that he has found the treasure and asks Jim to arrange a way home.

Jim returns to the loyal group at the stockade. The captain, doctor, squire, and their small party are preparing for an attack. Silver arrives to negotiate. He offers to spare them if they give him the map and surrender the ship. The captain refuses, so Silver’s men attack. The defenders hold the stockade, though they suffer losses. The doctor later goes out to treat wounded people, even though the pirates are still nearby.

Hands pretends to cooperate so Jim will help him steer the ship. Jim knows he cannot fully trust him, but the ship must be moved out of the pirates’ reach. He takes the wheel and watches Hands closely. His decision to act alone gives him a chance to help his friends, but it also places him in immediate danger.

Jim’s later decision to leave the stockade is risky and secretive. He hopes that moving the ship will help everyone, but he cannot know how dangerous Hands will be.

The Time Traveller explains that time is a dimension like length or height. His guests doubt him, so he shows them a small machine that can move through time. A week later, they return to his house and find him exhausted, dusty, and wearing strange clothes. He tells them that he has travelled far into the future. At first he watched the years pass from the machine, but he eventually reached a green world in the year 802,701. Small, gentle people called the Eloi lived among beautiful buildings. His curiosity became a practical problem: without the machine, he could not return home.

title: Frankenstein: A Request and a Refusal
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
Victor leaves home and travels alone, hoping that mountains and open air will calm him. On a glacier, the creature finds him and asks him to listen. title: Around the World in Eighty Days: A Wager and a Departure
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:

There they interrupt a ceremony and rescue Aouda, a young woman in danger. The rescue costs time, but Fogg refuses to leave her. The trip has already become more complicated than his timetable.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days: The Last Day
author: LessonCaptain (original retelling)
summary:
The group crosses the Atlantic on a ship whose captain will not take them to Liverpool. Fogg pays the crew to change course, but they run short of fuel and burn parts of the vessel. They finally reach Ireland and take a train to Liverpool. Fix arrests Fogg just before the party can continue to London. Soon afterward, a message confirms the real bank robber has been caught.
